title: Error Handling (throw / catch)
lead: Business errors are enum values declared by throws(E); omitted throws means Never. Propagation is explicit and checking is local. Panic remains a separate channel. These are target rules pending compiler and runtime implementation.

sections.heading: throw
sections.markdown: `throw expr` produces a business error directly and needs no extra try. Its enum value must satisfy the enclosing error declaration or an outer ordinary handler. Existing cleanup and owned pending-transfer rules apply; this does not select a platform unwinder or error ABI.

sections.heading: try / catch
sections.markdown: `try { ... } catch (e: ErrType) { ... }` handles errors locally; calls in its protected body need no individual marker. The region excludes nested function and closure bodies and that try statement's own handlers; a nested handler may still be protected by an outer try. Typed catches filter enum types; catch (e) binds Error. A bare uppercase-leading catch head is rejected with a suggestion to use catch (e: T). Remaining errors must fit the enclosing signature. A panic-only try also permits business calls but does not consume their errors: they must reach an outer ordinary catch or the function's throws, otherwise E0331. A handler cannot catch its own or a sibling handler's new error or panic.

sections.heading: catch panic
sections.markdown: The panic channel is separate from ordinary enum errors. Each try has at most one panic handler: `catch panic { ... }`, `catch panic (p) { ... }`, or `catch panic (p: PanicInfo) { ... }`. An annotation must be exactly PanicInfo. The binding is read-only and scoped to its handler; copies preserve class identity and do not imply Sendable. A handler protects only its try body, so a panic raised in a handler seeks an outer handler. The language PanicInfo class includes message, code, stack, cause and data. A panic escaping a cleanup boundary follows the independent terminal rule in spec 8.2.5.

sections.heading: Error propagation
sections.markdown: `try expr` propagates business errors, `try? expr` turns them into null, and `try! expr` turns them into a panic carrying the original error value. None converts cancellation or catches an independent panic. An expression marker with no business-error source is E0336. Any try block with an ordinary catch also needs a body source, even if it has a panic handler. A try with only a panic handler is exempt from that block-level check, including a pure body; inner expression markers are still checked. Direct throw counts as a source. An inner try?, try! or ordinary catch consuming an error does not erase the source fact in an outer body; E0336 is not dead-handler analysis. Unsubstituted generic E counts at definition time, but a caller's complete Never instantiation does not. try? preserves an already Optional result type without adding or recursively flattening layers; write (try? expr) ?? fallback. Entry-file top-level code permits errors but still requires call markers; main is an ordinary function and must declare its escaping errors. Callee signatures, not whole-program inference, determine escaping errors.

sections.heading: Debugger execution-flow boundaries
sections.markdown: Caught/uncaught debugger classification concerns the synchronous call chain of the current logical execution flow. A selected catch is caught; escape from the authenticated Instance or Task root is uncaught. A later await rethrow is classified in the awaiting flow. Observation precedes throw delivery and cleanup or handler effects. Registered generated-native code uses the current emitted protocol and owned registration. Resolved CALL primitives are copied after preparation, and actual child ENTER with exact binding/frame/thread proves admission before matching VM/native ancestors. Missing or old protocols reject before execution. Incomplete native origin coverage rejects all; incomplete handler routes reject caught/uncaught, preserving previous filters. All retains UNKNOWN for missing routes. Snapshots own native identity, Source coordinates and enum values without native locals or state, and continuation executes the original throw instruction once. Trusted canonical Source launch providers return same-proof native code, the current descriptor and a code lease, including native-only selections without unused VM entries. Receiving failures never fall back to VM; restart failure preserves the old stop, and detached execution retains its original code lease after adapter disposal. JSON stacks project authenticated Source coordinates without native locals or machine addresses. Native instruction breakpoints, startup pause with a native initializer or entry and native-only manual pause explicitly reject. Dynamic-library CLI loading, arbitrary native stepping and full safety qualification remain open.

sections.heading: defer must not let errors escape
sections.markdown: A cleanup body must statically have escaping error type Never (E0387). Use non-throwing APIs or handle errors inside the defer; no target runtime fallback accepts escaping business errors. Panic can be caught inside cleanup. Escape terminates uncatchably with status 70 during normal return, error, panic or cancellation cleanup; report the original panic code/message plus cleanup context and any in-flight outcome separately. CTFE instead fails the job as CLEANUP_PANIC without exiting the compiler. Runtime migration and validation remain pending.

sections.heading: Design principles
bullets: Errors are enum values and panic is a separate channel
Signatures and callable types carry throws(E); omission means Never
Check each body against declared signatures without whole-program error inference
Use typed errors for throwing public standard-library APIs; erased Error is forbidden in freestanding and @strict(alloc)
Use ADT enums for structured error causes and exhaustive match
